query: The Storm Run A storm is down on the lake, and a parcel must cross it tonight. The loft master looks at the jar at your belt, then at you. "Nobody else will go," she says. {flag(tailwind_fisherman) and flag(tailwind_gulls) and flag(tailwind_broom): You know how to let the wind get behind you.|You've never flown it in weather.} Open the jar and go You pull the stopper and the wind gets behind you and doesn't stop. You cross the lake faster than the lightning can find you. The parcel arrives dry. The wind stays with you after, when you call it. Halfway across, a gust takes you and you ditch in the shallows. The parcel survives. You barely do. The next storm season, the loft master says, you can try again. Wait for the lull, then go You wait, nerves screaming, for the gap in the storm, then open the jar and go. The wind gets behind you and stays. The parcel arrives an hour late and dry, and the wind is yours. The lull never comes, and you go anyway and ditch in the shallows. The next storm season, the loft master says.
